findings.title: Cache devices only after successful admission
findings.body: tagDeviceUI adds the device ID to the 29-minute cache before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, and leaves it cached when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Consequently, a new device's first request is rejected, but its next request hits the cache, returns nil, and authenticates successfully without being counted. Only cache successful admissions, so rejected devices cannot bypass the limit by retrying.

findings.title: The optional device header allows clients to bypass the limit
findings.body: Authenticate relies on TagDevice to enforce the limit, but TagDevice immediately returns nil when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Even when the configured limit is exhausted, an API client can omit this client-controlled header and receive an anonymous identity without any quota check. Enforcement needs an identifier clients cannot simply omit to opt out, such as a server-issued device cookie.

findings.title: Make the quota check and device insertion atomic
findings.body: CountDevices runs separately from the subsequent upsert, with no transaction or synchronization covering the admission decision. Concurrent requests for different new devices can all observe a count below deviceLimit and then all insert successfully, exceeding the configured limit. This also occurs across Grafana instances sharing the database. Serialize or atomically perform the quota check and insertion across database writers.

findings.title: Register the new setting for environment overrides
findings.body: The new device_limit key is not added to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana's environment-override pass visits keys already present in the loaded INI, while this read creates the missing key afterward. Setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone therefore leaves AnonymousDeviceLimit at zero and silently disables the limit unless device_limit is also declared in a configuration file. Add the key to the defaults or read it through an environment-aware configuration section.
